item.text: I’ve identified the integration points. I’m adding whitelist parsing that safely handles CIDRs and host:port inputs (including `@` for Unix sockets), creating/updating the header user and producing the same token fields as login, injecting successful auth into the UI config, and making redaction recursive for map values while preserving map keys.

The core path is now in place, but the Subsonic token must be generated in the same form the existing client expects; the browser’s normal flow derives it from the password, which proxy auth never receives. I’m checking the project’s Subsonic token conventions and frontend startup flow, then I’ll fix those details and compile/test the affected packages.

item.text:
Implemented reverse proxy authentication with configurable user header and IP whitelist, including CIDR, IP:port, IPv4/IPv6, and Unix socket `@` handling. Successful proxy logins create missing users, make the first user admin, update last login, and initialize the frontend session. Log redaction now handles nested map values while preserving keys.

Relevant tests passed: `go test ./server/app ./log ./conf`. Subsonic credentials are generated from the stored user password; users without a password receive an empty digest.
